title: The Harbor of Vilna
premise: In the port city of Vilna, where a crumbling empire's censors and revolutionaries both depend on Isandro Okonkwo's father's print shop, a dying courier leaves a swaddled child at their door along with a locked case of documents proving the governor-general has been selling condemned dissidents to foreign buyers. Isandro, who has survived by being invisible and useful, must carry the child and the evidence across three checkpoints — harbor, customs house, and the governor's own gate — before the new year's amnesty erases the crime forever. Betrayed by the one ally she trusted and forced to bargain with a censor who wants the evidence for himself, Isandro discovers the child is the governor's own granddaughter, abandoned to be silenced. In the end, she trades the documents not for money but for the child's safe passage abroad, keeps only one printed proof hidden inside a typecase, and watches the revolution she helped ignite consume the harbor she can no longer call home.
about_author: Astrid Yarrow is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes about the people history records only as margins — the hands that set the words others dared to print.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Isandro, sorting type in her father's shop, measures the city's unrest in confiscated pamphlets the censor brings weekly. POV Isandro. The beat is quiet dread: the world is tightening, and she has learned that survival means noticing everything and saying nothing.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: A bloodied courier dies on the shop's threshold, leaving a baby and a locked lead case with the words 'forget the face.' POV Isandro. The emotional beat is terror curdling into resolve as her father burns the courier's coat and they realize the shop is now a target.

chapters.title: What the Censor Reads
chapters.summary: Censor Aurel Voss arrives for his inspection and lingers too long, making clear he suspects them. Isandro opens the case alone at night: shipping manifests proving the governor-general traffics prisoners. POV Isandro. The beat is vertigo — knowledge as a weight that cannot be put down.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Isandro recruits Marek, a smuggler who owes her father, to move the case through the harbor checkpoint hidden in a type shipment. POV Marek. The beat is brittle camaraderie; Marek sees the price on their heads before Isandro admits it exists.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: The harbor crossing nearly fails when a guard recognizes the print shop's watermark on the crate; Marek bribes his way through, but a soldier memorizes Isandro's face. POV Isandro. The beat is the first taste of being seen — the thing she has spent her life avoiding.

chapters.title: The Governor's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: A locket sewn into the child's swaddling reveals her parentage, recasting everything: the governor left his own blood to be erased. Isandro's father urges giving the child back to save themselves. POV Isandro. The beat is the fracture between inheritance and conscience.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Voss intercepts them at customs, not to arrest but to bargain: he wants the documents to topple the governor and take his seat. He lets them pass as a loan, a leash. POV Voss. The beat is seduction of power — Isandro realizes she has handed a weapon to a patient man.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Print Shop
chapters.summary: Marek sells their route to the governor's men; the shop burns, her father is taken, and Isandro escapes with the child and one hidden folio of proofs sewn into her coat. POV Isandro. The beat is grief weaponized — the price of survival made literal in ash.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Governor's Gate
chapters.summary: On the century's last night, amid amnesty celebrations, Isandro walks through the governor's own gate carrying the evidence and the child, and confronts him with the one proof Voss doesn't know she kept. POV Isandro. The climax: she offers the documents in exchange for her father's life and the child's safe passage — and he, cornered by the crowd outside, accepts.

chapters.title: The Type That Remains
chapters.summary: Her father is released, broken; the child sails west with a trusted wet nurse; Voss rises on the evidence, and the revolution Isandro fueled remakes the harbor without her. She keeps a single cast letter — the first of the child's name — in an empty typecase. POV Isandro. The beat is bittersweet inheritance: she carried what mattered and let the rest burn.
